best: Power paths are drawn as real left-to-right paths with titled blocks and short notes: the 3V3 buck, the 5 V buck, the four-switch stage with its shunts and cap banks, and the pack fuse/back-to-back FET path all read like textbook drawings.
worst: USB sheets have several parts drawn on top of each other so refs/values are unreadable: D410 over C410, D411 over C458, R415 over TH401, C417 over C418, R403 over C404, R417/R435 text on their own bodies (also C118 and R113 on the Cells sheet).

Sparse, unbalanced pages with stranded parts: EEPROM U402, Q409 (V9_EN switch), Q103, TP412 and the CE_N divider sit alone far from what they serve, tied only by labels, with large empty regions around them.

Charger and gauge pins fan out through long staircase wires that end in a label (gate drives, FB/FBG, ACUV/ACOV, VC1-4), so checking against the datasheet still means hopping by net name to the power stage and sense blocks.
